```{r, include = FALSE}
# built.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`convert_person_id()` runs the BEF conversion procedures in `DB_PSD`. You
choose a procedure and give it a set of `PNR`s or `PERSON_ID`s. You get the
procedure's output table back as a data frame, or saved as an Oracle table.

This vignette gives one example per procedure family. The method behind the
procedures is described in "Metodevejledning konvertering mellem cpr og
person_id" (K22, `G:\k22\01 Metode\Diskretionering\Pseudonymisering`).

```{r}
library(DSTutils)
```

## Two kinds of time

Every row in the BEF tables has two periods:

* **Validity** (`VFRA`–`VTIL`): when the link between `PNR` and `PERSON_ID`
  held in reality.
* **Registry** (`RFRA`–`RTIL`): when the registry recorded it that way.
  Corrections close the old row in registry time and add a new one.

The date arguments pick rows from these periods:

| You want | Procedure family | Date arguments |
|---|---|---|
| The ids as known today | current (`AKTUEL*`, `BEF_OMKOD`) | none |
| The ids valid on a date, as known today | current | `validity_date` |
| The ids valid on a date, as known at a given time | historic (`HISTORISK*`) | `validity_date`, optionally `registry_time` |
| Every version within a registry interval | full history (`FULD_HIS*`) | none, or `registry_start_time` + `registry_end_time` |

Use the historic procedures to reproduce an earlier extract. If you give
only `validity_date`, the registry time is set to the first delivery that
covers that date (from `D101200.bef_leverance_time`).

Other combinations are an error. The error message lists what the procedure
accepts.

## Current ids

```{r}
pnr <- data.frame(PNR = c("0101011234", "0202024321"))

# PERSON_ID as known today
ids <- convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_AKTUELLE_ID",
  in_table_name = pnr,
  project_id = "D101200"
)

# PNR valid on 31 December 2021, as known today
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_AKTUELLE_PNR",
  in_table_name = data.frame(PERSON_ID = ids$PERSON_ID),
  project_id = "D101200",
  validity_date = 31122021
)
```

For the most common case, adding `PERSON_ID` to a data frame with `PNR`,
use `add_person_id()`. It sends only the distinct PNRs and drops `PNR` from
the result (set `drop_pnr = FALSE` to keep it):

```{r}
my_data <- data.frame(pnr = c("0101011234", "0101011234"), income = c(1, 2))
add_person_id(my_data)
```

## Historic ids

```{r}
pid <- data.frame(PERSON_ID = ids$PERSON_ID)

# Valid on 31 December 2021, as known at the first delivery after that date
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_HISTORISK_PNR",
  in_table_name = pid,
  project_id = "D101200",
  validity_date = 31122021
)

# ... or as known at a time you choose
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_HISTORISK_PNR",
  in_table_name = pid,
  project_id = "D101200",
  validity_date = 31122021,
  registry_time = "16012022 18:00:00"
)
```

## Full history

```{r}
# All versions
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_FULD_HISTORIK_ID",
  in_table_name = pid,
  project_id = "D101200"
)

# Only versions recorded within a registry interval
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_FULD_HISTORIK_ID",
  in_table_name = pid,
  project_id = "D101200",
  registry_start_time = "01012020 00:00:00",
  registry_end_time = "31122021 23:59:59"
)
```

The `KOEN_FOEDSELSDAG` procedures (sex and birthday for a `PERSON_ID`) come
in the same three families and take the same date arguments.

## PERSON_ID shifts and invalid ids

```{r}
# Which PERSON_IDs have been replaced, and by what
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_IDSKIFT",
  in_table_name = pid,
  project_id = "D101200"
)

# Invalid ids; takes no input table
convert_person_id(procedure = "BEF_INVALIDE", project_id = "D101200")
```

## Tables in Oracle

The input can be an Oracle table and the output can be saved as one. The ids
then don't have to pass through R. Only the distinct values of the id column
are used:

```{r}
# Input and output in a project schema on another database
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_IDSKIFT",
  in_data = "ORACLE",
  in_table_name = "D222401.PERSON_ID_TABEL",
  in_database = "STATPROD",
  out_data = "ORACLE",
  out_table_name = "IDSKIFT_2024",
  out_database = "STATPROD",
  proxy = "D222401",
  project_id = "D222401"
)

# Input in DB_PSD, id column with another name, output kept in your
# DB_PSD schema
convert_person_id(
  procedure = "BEF_OMKOD",
  in_data = "ORACLE",
  in_table_name = "MIN_TABEL",
  column_name = "CPR_NR",
  out_data = "ORACLE",
  out_table_name = "MIN_TABEL_ID",
  project_id = "D101200"
)
```

A table kept in `DB_PSD` stays until you drop it. If it holds CPR numbers,
drop it as soon as you are done.

## Pitfalls

* **PNR must be text.** A PNR stored as a number has lost the leading zero of
  days 01-09 and will not be found. You get a warning; convert first with
  `sprintf("%010.0f", PNR)`.
* **Ids that are not found** come back as `PNR = "Ukendt-PNR"` or
  `PERSON_ID = 999999999999999`.
* **One run at a time per user.** Runs share the input work table
  `BEF_ID_PROC` in your `DB_PSD` schema.
